question: What is the outermost layer of the skin called?
explanation: The epidermis is the outermost, superficial layer of the skin made of epithelial tissue. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h1)

question: Where is the hypodermis located in relation to the main skin layers?
explanation: The hypodermis lies directly beneath the dermis to anchor the skin to underlying tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h1)

question: What skin pigment protects cells from ultraviolet light damage?
explanation: Melanin is produced by melanocytes to absorb harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main role of Langerhans cells in the epidermis?

options.A: Sensing touch and pressure changes in the environment
options.B: Fighting off invading pathogens and alerting the immune system
options.C: Producing waterproof oils to keep the skin surface soft
options.D: Storing excess fat for padding and insulation

explanation: Langerhans cells act as immune sentinels in the skin to catch invaders and trigger a defense response. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h2)

question: What happens to dermal blood vessels when a person becomes very hot?

options.A: They pump more sweat directly into the skin
options.B: They constrict to trap heat in the body core
options.C: They dilate to release heat through the skin
options.D: They close completely to stop all blood flow

explanation: Vasodilation brings warm blood near the surface so excess body heat can escape into the air. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h3)

question: A patient has a high fever and flushed, warm skin. Which process is the body using to cool down?
explanation: The body responds to high heat by widening blood vessels and producing sweat to promote heat loss. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which skin receptors are primarily responsible for detecting light touch?
explanation: Meissner's corpuscles are specialized nerve endings located close to the skin surface that sense light touch. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why is sensory reception in the skin vital for overall physical safety?

options.A: It produces essential vitamins when exposed to sunlight
options.B: It warns the brain about dangerous pressure, heat, or injury
options.C: It controls how fast the outer layer of skin cells grows
options.D: It regulates the amount of water lost through the pores

explanation: Sensory receptors detect environmental hazards like extreme heat or sharp pressure so the body can react quickly. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h4)

question: What environmental factor triggers the skin to start producing vitamin D?

options.B: Direct physical pressure on the palms
options.C: High humidity levels in the air
options.D: Cold winter wind blowing on the face

explanation: Sunlight provides the ultraviolet energy needed to transform skin molecules into a vitamin D precursor. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is vitamin D production in the skin important for bone health?

options.A: It increases red blood cell production in marrow
options.B: It lubricates the joints to prevent stiffness
options.C: It helps the digestive tract absorb calcium properly
options.D: It keeps the skin surface strong and waterproof

explanation: Active vitamin D is essential for the intestines to absorb dietary calcium, which keeps bones strong. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the oily substance produced by sebaceous glands called?
explanation: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum, an oily substance that conditions the skin and hair. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which waste products are eliminated from the body through sweat?

options.B: Red blood cells and blood platelets
options.D: Salt, water, and small amounts of urea

explanation: Sweat contains mostly water and salt, along with minor metabolic waste products like urea. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h6)

question: How does the skin act as a blood reservoir during strenuous exercise?

options.A: Sweat glands pull extra blood out through the pores
options.B: Subcutaneous fat pumps blood back to the heart
options.C: The epidermis stores extra blood cells in dead layers
options.D: Dermal vessels constrict to send blood to active muscles

explanation: Constricting blood vessels in the skin shifts stored blood toward exercising muscles and vital organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which property of the skin allows patches and creams to deliver medication into the body?

options.A: High concentration of sweat and oil glands
options.B: Continuous shedding of the outer epidermis
options.D: Thick layer of insulating subcutaneous fat

explanation: Certain medications can pass through the skin barrier because the skin is semi-permeable to fat-soluble compounds. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h7)

question: A nurse notices that a patient's skin is very dry and lacks normal turgor. Which physiological issue does this most likely suggest?
explanation: Poor skin turgor and dryness are classic clinical signs of fluid loss and dehydration. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why is the skin considered a window into a patient's general health status?

options.A: It is the only body organ that nurses can touch easily
options.B: The skin produces all the hormones needed to run the body
options.C: Skin cells grow faster than any other cells in the body
options.D: Changes in skin color and texture often reflect internal organ problems

explanation: Systemic illnesses frequently show visible signs on the skin, such as jaundice for liver issues or pallor for anemia. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)
